summary: Today’s pulse tracks Parts of England under heat alert with 30C possible, India ‘cockroach’ activist ends hunger strike after 26 days as protests spread, and Middle East crisis latest: US carries out strikes across Iran as Tehran targets American bases in region. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are across, south, and burnham. In the background, Andy Burnham spends first working day at new No 10 North in Manchester – UK politics live and France evacuates Cap Ferret peninsula as Spanish wildfires merge near Madrid – Europe live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Parts of England under heat alert with 30C possible
headlines.description: Warning in place until Sunday morning in southern and central regions after drought declared in parts of Wales Heat alerts are in place across parts of England, with officials saying temperatures are likely to have an impact on health and wellbeing. The yellow heat health alerts issued for the East Midlands, east of England, London, south-east, south-west and West Midlands are in place until 9am on Sunday.

headlines.title: India ‘cockroach’ activist ends hunger strike after 26 days as protests spread
headlines.description: Sonam Wangchuk halts strike after receiving assurances parliament will address protesters’ concerns about exam system The Indian “cockroach” activist Sonam Wangchuk has ended a 26-day hunger strike, as youth-led protests continued to erupt across the country and leaders of the movement said there was no breakthrough in talks with the government. Wangchuk had been fasting since June in solidarity with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), a new youth-led movement that has been holding mass protests calling for government accountability and the resignation of the education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, over exam paper leaks. The leaks affected 2 million students in May and have been linked to more than a dozen suicides.

headlines.title: Middle East crisis latest: US carries out strikes across Iran as Tehran targets American bases in region
headlines.description: Latest attacks come after Trump vowed ‘major military punishment’ for Tehran and its Houthi allies US missiles struck targets across Iran on Friday after Donald Trump vowed “major military punishment” for Tehran and its Houthi allies in Yemen for extending the Middle East war to a second major shipping chokepoint, the mouth of the ⁠Red Sea. The US Central Command said it targeted Iranian military command centres, communication networks, drone storage facilities, coastal surveillance sites and maritime capabilities.

headlines.title: Andy Burnham spends first working day at new No 10 North in Manchester – UK politics live
headlines.description: PM, on his first day at new base, says it will create ‘that sense of a more balanced country, that big things can be done from here’ Andy Burnham has arrived by police convoy at No 10 North at Heron House in Manchester: Andy Burnham was probably feeling left out of the “Celtic alliance”, after apparently telling John Swinney that Scottish independence was “off limits”.

headlines.title: France evacuates Cap Ferret peninsula as Spanish wildfires merge near Madrid – Europe live
headlines.description: French evacuees using hundreds of mobilised boats or the only road linking the area with the mainland as evacuation also ordered in areas near Spanish capital Over in France, it’s not just the south-west that gets affected, but the country’s south-east regions are also being hard hit, AFP noted. Dozens of fires flared up and are being fanned by the mistral wind around the historic village of Cotignac – officials saying around 25 houses had been destroyed since Tuesday.

headlines.title: From high heels to ‘Zara death pants’: how fashion falls foul of women’s safety
headlines.description: A physio, a tailor and a historian on the style trends that can put women in hospital and how to avoid the dangers “Buyer beware” is one of the oldest principles in English law. Now, a pair of wide legged trousers from Zara is bringing the phrase back to the forefront of shoppers’ minds. On social media the £25.99 wide-legged trousers from the high-street retailer have earned the moniker “Zara death pants” thanks to a slew of videos showing wearers tripping over the leg of the trousers and injuring themselves.

headlinePool.title: Justice Elena Kagan decries idea that US supreme court ‘rubber-stamps’ Trump’s agenda
headlinePool.description: Kagan rejects notion that high court ‘does whatever the administration wants’, pointing to tariffs ruling and more Liberal justice Elena Kagan has said it was “wrong” to accuse the US supreme court of becoming a rubber stamp for Donald Trump in his second term, amid criticism of its authorization of some of the president’s most controversial actions. Pointing to rulings against the president on key issues such as tariffs, Kagan – one of three liberals on a court that has in recent years been defined by rulings authored by members of its six-justice conservative majority – defended it at an annual gathering of attorneys and judges for the ninth judicial circuit in Bellevue, Washington, on Thursday.

headlinePool.title: Southport killer Axel Rudakubana is manipulating system, victims’ families say
headlinePool.description: Rudakubana moved to psychiatric hospital after it was concluded he could not be safely managed in prison The Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has been accused of attempting to “manipulate the system” by the families of his victims, after it emerged he had been transferred from prison to a psychiatric hospital. Rudakubana, 19, was jailed for life in January last year, with a minimum sentence of 52 years, for the murders of Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, Bebe King, six, and nine-year-old Alice da Silva Aguiar.

headlinePool.title: Canadian government urged to block data-sharing deal between Thomson Reuters and US ICE
headlinePool.description: ICE will pay Canadian media giant US$125m to use its investigative database to identify ‘immigration fraud’ A Canadian federal opposition party leader is calling on the Mark Carney government to block the latest data-sharing deal between US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and the Canadian media giant Thomson Reuters. Avi Lewis, the federal leader of the New Democratic party (NDP), demanded on Tuesday that Ottawa address the contract and further restrict Canadian corporations from doing business with ICE, after Canada’s National Observer reported on the deal.

headlinePool.title: Judge orders Hegseth to explain US military’s new testosterone policy
headlinePool.description: Court questions plan to offer male hormone treatment to cisgender troops while denying it to trans service members Pete Hegseth’s controversial plan to screen older soldiers for testosterone deficiencies and offer them more of the hormone faced scrutiny this week from a federal judge, who ordered the Trump administration to explain a discrepancy with the treatment of transgender troops. The US defense secretary announced earlier this month that male service members aged 30 and above would be checked to ensure they have the “right testosterone levels” to perform in the military at an optimal level.

headlinePool.title: Poland’s main rightwing opposition splits after loyalty pledge ultimatum
headlinePool.description: Former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki and allies say they were forced out over factional disagreements Poland’s main opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party has split, after former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki and his allies said they were forced out over factional disagreements on policy direction ahead of next year’s parliamentary election. Speaking at a press conference, the party’s longtime leader , Jarosław Kaczyński, said dozens of members of parliament effectively left the party after refusing to sign a loyalty oath.

headlinePool.title: A former nun explains why she ran away from her 'Cloistered' life
headlinePool.description: Catherine Coldstream entered a Carmelite monastery at age 24, and lived a life of prayer and obedience for 12 years. Her memoir is C loistered: My Years as a Nun. Originally published March 20, 2024.

headlinePool.title: Four men in 20s die after car crashes into lamp-post in Merseyside
headlinePool.description: Police appeal for witnesses after collision in Huyton leaves four men dead and a fifth in hospital Four men in their 20s have died after a car crash in Merseyside in the early hours of Friday. Police were called just before 2am to reports that a black Seat Cupra had left the road and collided with a lamp-post in Huyton. The car was travelling from Liverpool towards Knowsley.

headlinePool.title: Woman and man arrested in Ireland after police intercept ‘highly sophisticated’ bomb
headlinePool.description: Detectives targeting dissident republicans stopped a vehicle containing explosives near Carrickmacross Two people have been arrested after police in Ireland targeting dissident republicans intercepted an “extremely significant” bomb that was being transported in a vehicle near the border. Members of the Garda Síochána’s special detective unit stopped the vehicle travelling on the N2 south of Carrickmacross, County Monaghan on Wednesday afternoon.

headlinePool.title: Indonesian babies were trafficked to Singapore. What happens to them now?
headlinePool.description: At least 12 babies have been trafficked from Indonesia to Singapore, but what will happen to them remains unclear.
